title: Expose repairs and resynchronization instead of silently discarding data
finding: Remux records errors/gap skips and performs bounded timestamp/configuration repairs, but there is no uniform input/output-range repair ledger in the inspected native/JS interface. Existing typed route errors distinguish interruption from incompatibility; they do not account for every repaired field or skipped byte.
novelty: New diagnostic/fidelity home. R131 repair search, R311 trusted corruption repair and codec-specific normalization do not own cross-operation repair provenance.
next_action: Start with existing AAC timestamp and AVC/HEVC DTS repairs: emit bounded reason/source-epoch/input-output identities with unchanged-media controls. Then inject junk, truncated init and inconsistent metadata; distinguish strict rejection, requested salvage and live concealment before broadening.
reopen_condition: Do not turn a permissive parser into an automatic arbitrary-file fixer. Avoid implementing validation rules that cannot be sourced or independently checked.

proposal_contract.Proposed mechanism: Every skip, repaired field, inferred duration or rejected metadata element has an explicit reason and input/output range. Separate strict-file fidelity, explicit salvage and live concealment policies.
proposal_contract.Smallest useful experiment: Inject junk between audio frames, malformed EBML sizes, truncated initialization and metadata disagreements. Compare strict, diagnostic and opt-in repair paths.
proposal_contract.Correctness gate: No silent data loss classified as preservation; unchanged path remains byte-identical when valid; repair budget bounded; unsupported semantics return an explicit outcome.
proposal_contract.Measure only after correctness: Correct admission, trustworthy diagnostics and fewer hidden fidelity failures; validation overhead measured separately.

upstream_evidence: Imported 2026-09-21 source review, not fetched or revalidated in this run.
